# The Motley Fool

> Stock investing research, market news, and personal finance from The Motley Fool.

fool.com publishes investing analysis, stock quotes, educational articles, and podcasts. This file is a short map of the public site for AI agents.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.fool.com/): Featured investing stories and market coverage
- [Stock quotes](https://www.fool.com/quote/): Quote lookup, charts, and company data
- [Investing news](https://www.fool.com/investing-news/): Latest investing articles
- [Trending news](https://www.fool.com/trending-news/): Popular market stories
- [Podcasts](https://www.fool.com/podcasts/): Show list and episodes
- [Authors](https://www.fool.com/author/): Author directory
- [Calculators](https://www.fool.com/calculators/index/): Personal finance calculators
- [How to invest](https://www.fool.com/investing/how-to-invest/): Investing education
- [Financial terms](https://www.fool.com/terms/): Glossary of investing and finance terms
- [Research](https://www.fool.com/research/): Data-driven analysis and financial statistics
- [Markets](https://www.fool.com/markets/): Market data tables and stock performance lists
- [Stock market basics](https://www.fool.com/investing/stock-market/): Evergreen investing articles
- [Slideshows](https://www.fool.com/slideshow/): Visual investing guides
- [About](https://www.fool.com/about/): Company information
- [Legal](https://www.fool.com/legal/terms-and-conditions/): Terms and legal pages

## Notes

- Quote pages use `/quote/{exchange}/{symbol}/` (example: [/quote/nasdaq/aapl/](https://www.fool.com/quote/nasdaq/aapl/)).
- Article URLs often include a date: `/{section}/YYYY/MM/DD/{slug}/`.
- Podcast shows use `/podcasts/{show}/` and episodes use `/podcasts/{show}/{YYYY-MM-DD}-{slug}/` (example: [/podcasts/hidden-gems/](https://www.fool.com/podcasts/hidden-gems/)).
- Earnings call transcripts use `/earnings/call-transcripts/YYYY/MM/DD/{slug}/`.

Common Questions

The Motley Fool is an investment research company founded in 1993 by brothers Tom and David Gardner, with a purpose to make the world smarter, happier, and richer. We help individual investors make better investing decisions and build wealth for the long term.

Fool.com offers free investing news, analysis, and education for everyone, while our premium services provide members with official Motley Fool stock recommendations, portfolio strategies, insights from experienced Motley Fool investment analysts, and proprietary AI-powered investment research tools and data.

The Motley Fool's free articles, podcasts, and videos are available to everyone on Fool.com. They're designed to help you understand the stock market, research potential investments, and become a smarter long-term investor.

Premium services go further. Members get official Motley Fool stock recommendations, in-depth investment research, stock rankings, portfolio strategies, and ongoing investing guidance from dedicated teams of Motley Fool investment analysts. Members also get access to proprietary investing tools that combine analyst expertise with quantitative data and AI. Depending on the service, members may also get real-money portfolios and more robust financial planning resources from our Certified Financial Planners.

In short, our free content helps you learn, research, and make sense of stock market news. Our premium services help you decide what to invest in and build a long-term portfolio.

Founded more than 30 years ago, The Motley Fool has worked to level the playing field for individual investors by giving them the research, tools, education, and community to make more informed investing decisions.

Whether you're just getting started or have been investing for years, we can help you learn to evaluate investments, understand the companies you own and the ones on your watchlist, build a diversified portfolio, and stay focused through market ups and downs.

We believe in investing for the long term. When we recommend a stock, we generally do so with the intention of holding it for at least five years, giving great businesses time to grow and helping individual investors look beyond short-term market noise. We also believe in diversification, typically building toward a portfolio of 50 or more individual stocks to spread risk across different companies, sectors, and opportunities.

You can start with our free articles, podcasts, investing guides, and YouTube videos. Premium members get access to official Motley Fool stock recommendations, in-depth investment research, stock rankings, portfolio strategies, proprietary investing tools, and insights from our investment analyst teams.

Watch and Learn

Tom Gardner's 5 Rules for Long-Term Investors in the AI Era

Five practical rules for long-term equity investors adapting to AI-driven structural change. Tom Gardner explains how to redesign portfolios and research processes for multi-year compounding. He recommends holding at least 50 individual stocks to reduce single-name and industry risk, spending about half your research time with generative AI tools (while validating their outputs), and reweighting away from legacy software toward AI infrastructure and capital-intensive enablers. He also urges investors to codify their time horizon, volatility tolerance, cash buffers, and position sizing each year, and to keep short-term speculative money out of the core portfolio in favor of 5+ year horizons.
